title: Each failure points to a different repair
caption: Match the remedy to the failed evidence, rather than asking for a more confident explanation.
points: Voltage needs an adequate model. Restoration needs the current network and service policy.
Cyber response needs justified independent evidence. A new explanation alone repairs none of these.
note: Return to the opening comparison. A broader AC violation requires a candidate change, broader model study, or both. A changed network or rating invalidates restoration evidence until the affected study is repeated. A stealth measurement change requires an independent trust argument or escalation; a quiet residual does not supply it. Each repair is a concrete engineering step. The LLM can help interpret a request, assemble the right tool arguments and explain verified results, but it cannot substitute wording for missing evidence. Ask for one example from each case without adding another timed exercise.

title: An operator reviews one complete recommendation packet
caption: Illustrative advisory handoff. Local acknowledgment records review and does not dispatch equipment.
points: Show the proposed action, expected benefit, checked limits, failed checks and remaining uncertainty.
Bind the reviewer’s readback to the same case, candidate and evidence version.
note: A useful packet lets an operator inspect why a candidate is eligible for review. It includes what the solver actually checked and what remains outside the model. Voltage should show model scope and margins. Restoration should identify the served and unserved demand and the need for operational isolation/protection work. Cyber should identify the trusted evidence assumption and the response audit. The classroom acknowledgment checks a packet identity and operator name. That local interaction has no connection to live SCADA or DMS control. In deployment, the utility’s operating procedures, role permissions, interlocks and field coordination remain separate engineering requirements.

title: A useful pilot measures completed work and its errors
points: Compare against the same numerical tools and a strong fixed workflow, under matched task and time budgets.
Measure correct completed tasks, missed limits, stale evidence, reviewer effort and total elapsed time.
Retain failures, input versions and decisions so another engineer can reproduce the finding.
note: Close with a testable motivation for agentic assistance: reducing specific workflow errors or handling varied requests without weakening numerical checks. The recorded voltage selector tied voting, so the tutorial makes no blanket claim that a learned selector improves every task. The restoration improvement in critical service came from objective weights, and the cyber recovery benefit came from protected measurements. A pilot should isolate what the agent adds under matched conditions. If the question concerns human workload, use a human study instead of inferring workload from solver seconds. The teaching guide contains all three exercise debriefs, full primary references, numerical provenance and local evidence paths.
